claims.statement: The root joined to six centers with pendant-leaf counts (3,3,3,3,3,2) is an ordinary 24-vertex tree with a vertex cover of size 6; at p=10 it lies in n=2p+4 and satisfies x=8, alpha=18, x+2<=p, and 3p<2alpha+1. All 17 original leaves are strictly favorable and its complete aggregate is S=-122805. Consequently tau(T)>=7 is not a universal property of eligible trees in this slice.
claims.scope: This exact tree only. It disproves a universal claim that every eligible n=2p+4 tree has tau(T)>=7. It does not disprove a conditional theorem restricted to trees with tau(T)>=7, refute the primary aggregate, or decide other ranks or trees.
claims.reason: retained_narrowed: the graph, cover, eligibility, strict selector, every summand, and full negative sum replay exactly. The original implication is narrowed because a low-cover witness refutes universality of the premise tau>=7 but cannot by itself refute a conditional implication that assumes tau>=7.

limitations: Selector and per-leaf summand replay used the pinned ordinary_tree_checked.py evaluator; no second implementation was run for every leaf-deleted polynomial.
The witness has negative S and does not refute the primary lower-region aggregate.
The witness rules out only a universal tau(T)>=7 assertion for this slice; no conditional theorem on the tau(T)>=7 subclass was tested.
No exhaustive low-cover classification or general pointwise sign result was established.
